Here is a concise, stand-alone 12-week program summary you can hand to a client or keep as a reference for planning with your trainee. It integrates the strength plan, phased progression, anti-inflammatory nutrition, cardio, abs work tailored to a prior L4–L5 herniation, sleep and recovery protocol, and the 1RM testing plan in Week 12. The summary is organized by phase, with week-by-week structure, exercise selections, sets/reps, and key coaching notes.

Overall goals and safety
- Primary goals: build general strength, improve movement quality, increase work capacity, and support back health with spine-neutral loading and anti-inflammatory nutrition.
- Back health rules: maintain neutral spine, brace during all lifts, avoid loaded spinal flexion, and minimize heavy spinal flexion movements. Use safer deadlift hinges (Romanian/trap-bar) and posture-friendly squats (back/front as suitable).
- Training frequency: 4 days/week lifting + 2 cardio sessions/week (on non-consecutive days or after lifting as schedule permits).
- Recovery emphasis: 7–9 hours sleep, 2.5–3.5 L water, protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day, anti-inflammatory foods, 10–20 minutes post-workout mobility, and regular deloads in Week 4, 8, 12 as appropriate.

Phase 1: Foundation and patterning (Weeks 1–4)
Goals: establish movement quality, spine-bracing, and safe loading; build endurance in core and hips; begin anti-inflammatory nutrition and cardio base.

Weekly structure
- Day A: Upper Body Push/Pull (horizontal emphasis) + core
  - Bench Press: 3x8
  - Seated Row: 3x10
  - Overhead Dumbbell Press: 3x10
  - Dumbbell Incline Flyes: 3x12
  - Pallof Press: 3x12 per side
  - Band External Rotation: 2x15 per side
- Day B: Lower Body Strength
  - Goblet Squat: 3x12
  - Romanian Deadlift: 3x12
  - Split Squat: 3x10 per leg
  - Glute Bridge/Hip Thrust: 3x12
  - Plank: 3x30–45s
  - Farmer’s Walk: 2x30s
- Day C: Upper Body Pull
  - Pull-Ups/Lat Pulldown: 3x8–10
  - Barbell Row: 3x8
  - Face Pull: 3x12
  - Dumbbell Curls: 2x12
  - Z-Press (seated): 3x10
  - Anti-rotation Side Plank: 2x30s per side
- Day D: Mobility/Conditioning
  - Hip/Thoracic mobility: 10–15 minutes
  - Turkish Get-Up or progressions: 2x4 per side
  - Pallof/Anti-rotation work: 3x12 per side
  - 15–20 minutes cardio (bike/row)

Abs/core (throughout Phase 1)
- Phase 1 core: Pallof Press, Plank, Side Plank, Dead Bug, Bird Dog, Farmer’s Walk
- Frequency: 2–3 x per week as add-ons or integrated on Days A/B

Cardio
- 2 sessions/week, 20–25 minutes each, Zone 2–3

Phase 2: Hypertrophy and strength emphasis with push intensity (Weeks 5–8)
Goals: push intensity safely; increase pushing volume and loads while maintaining core stability and back health.

Week 5
- Day A (Horizontal Push/Pull)
  - Barbell Bench Press: 4x6–8 (increase load ~2.5–5% from Week 4)
  - Barbell Row or Dumbbell Row: 4x8
  - Dumbbell Overhead Press: 3x8
  - Chest-Supported Incline DB Press: 3x10
  - Pallof Press: 3x12 per side
  - External Rotation: 2x12
- Day B (Lower Strength/Hypertrophy)
  - Back Squat or Front Squat: 4x6–8
  - Romanian Deadlift: 3x8–10
  - Bulgarian Split Squat: 3x8 per leg
  - Hip Thrust/Glute Bridge: 3x10–12
  - Core: 3x45–60s planks
  - Farmer’s Walk: 2x40s
- Day C (Vertical/Horizontal Pull)
  - Pull-Ups/Lat Pulldown: 4x6–8
  - T-Bar/Dumbbell Row: 4x8
  - Face Pull: 3x12
  - Barbell Curls: 3x8–10
  - DB Lateral Raises: 3x12
  - Pallof Press: 3x12 per side
- Day D: Mobility/Conditioning
  - Mobility work + 20–25 minutes light cardio

Week 6
- Similar to Week 5 with +2.5–5% load where form allows; keep reps stable

Week 7
- Push intensity ramp continues; start slight overloads on top sets
  - Bench: 4–5x5–6 at 85–90% of Week 5–6 load
  - Row: 4x6–8
  - Overhead Press: 3–4x6–8
  - Chest-Supported Incline: 3x8–10
  - Pallof Press: 4x12 per side
- Lower/Posterior chain and core maintain volumes

Week 8
- Return to higher volume with slightly higher reps or sets
  - Bench: 4x6–8
  - Row: 4x8
  - Press: 3x8
  - Squat: 4x6–8
  - RDL: 3x8–10
  - Hip/Glute work + core: 3–4 exercises

Phase 3: Strength consolidation and conditioning toward 1RM testing (Weeks 9–12)
Goals: consolidate gains, prepare for 1RM test in Week 12 with safe ramping.

Weeks 9–10
- Week 9
  - Day A: Bench Press 5x5 @ 75–85%
  - Day B: Back Squat 5x5 @ 75–85%
  - Day C: Pull/Row patterns + core
  - Day D: Mobility/conditioning
- Week 10
  - Day A: Bench 4x4–5x4 @ 80–90%
  - Day B: Squat 4x4–5x4 @ 80–90%
  - Day C: Accessory work; anti-rotation core
  - Day D: Cardio as tolerated

Weeks 11–12
- Week 11
  - Day A: Bench variant 3x3–4x3 at 85–92% or 3–4x2–3 at ~92–97% if form is pristine
  - Day B: Squat variant 3x3–4x3 at 85–92%
  - Day C: Light pulling/accessory; maintain core work
  - Day D: Mobility and light conditioning
- Week 12 (1RM testing week)
  - Warm-up protocol for the chosen lift (bench or squat)
  - Gradual progression:
    - 5–8 minutes light cardio
    - Sets: 8 reps at ~50%, 6 reps at 60–70%, 3 reps at 75–80%, 2 reps at 85–90%, 1 rep at 95%
    - Then single attempts with 5–10 kg/10–20 lb jumps
  - If testing more than one lift, test on separate days with at least 48–72 hours between tests
  - Post-test: deload/recovery plan and nutrition emphasis to recover

Abs/core integration
- Phase 1: 2–3 sessions/week
- Phase 2: maintain with slight load increases; keep 2–3 core sessions/week
- Phase 3: maintain core work; reduce volume slightly in Week 11 to manage fatigue

Cardio
- 2 sessions/week: 20–40 minutes depending on phase
- Early phase: 20–25 minutes
- Phase 2: 25–35 minutes
- Phase 3: 30–40 minutes; one session may include optional light intervals if tolerated

Anti-inflammatory nutrition (summary)
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day
- Carbs: 3–5 g/kg/day depending on load
- Fats: remaining calories from unsaturated fats with omega-3 emphasis
- Anti-inflammatory foods: fatty fish 2–3x/week, olive oil, leafy greens, berries, cruciferous vegetables, turmeric/ginger, garlic/onions, probiotic foods
- Supplements: omega-3s (1–3 g/day EPA/DHA), turmeric/curcumin (500–1000 mg/day), vitamin D as needed, magnesium 200–400 mg/day, probiotics as needed
- Hydration: 2.5–3.5 L/day, more on training days

Sleep and recovery protocol (summary)
- Sleep: 7–9 hours per night, consistent schedule
- Pre-sleep routine: lights down, mobility, box breathing (4x4)
- Sleep environment: cool, dark, quiet
- Naps: 20–25 minutes if needed
- Recovery practices: 10–20 minutes post-workout mobility, 2–3 mobility sessions weekly, light cardio to enhance recovery
- Desk/work strategy: ergonomic setup, frequent movement breaks
- Supplements: magnesium before bed if needed; vitamin D if deficient; Omega-3s; probiotics as per appetite

Testing and progression notes
- Week 12 1RM test protocol provided; choose 1–2 primary lifts to test
- Week 11 taper and Week 12 testing plan ensure safety and technique
- Back health guards: if pain or numbness appears, stop and revert to submaximal loads; consult clinician as needed

Progress tracking and coaching cues
- Use RPE targets for progression (Weeks 5–8: RPE 8–9 on top sets; Weeks 9–11: taper with consistent technique; Week 12: max attempts)
- Focus on bracing, neutral spine, scapular retraction and stable ribcage
- Use a log to track:
  - Lift weights, reps, sets
  - RPE
  - Any back symptoms
  - Sleep duration/quality
  - Nutrition adherence and protein target
  - Cardio tolerance and recovery

What you’ll need to finalize
- If you want, I can convert this into a week-by-week workbook with exact weights, progression tables based on Week 11 numbers, and a detailed 1RM testing day protocol (including warm-ups, rest times, and safety cues). I can also deliver a printable one-page plan for client handout.

- A concise, client-facing handout version of the 12-week plan with simple tables you can print?

- Non-exercise recovery activities (2–3 per week, easy to moderate intensity):
  - 15–20 minutes of mobility flow targeting hips, thoracic spine, and shoulders after workouts.

  - 5–10 minutes of low-intensity cardio or mobility work after heavy sessions to promote blood flow and lactate clearance.

  - 2–3 times per week: 5–12 minutes of spinal decompression or neutral spine cues (prone press-up, bird-dog progressions, dead bug).

  - Ergonomic chair with lumbar support; chair height that keeps feet flat and knees at 90 degrees.

  - Short productive micro-mounters every 60–90 minutes: 20–40 seconds of hip hinge, 1–2 bodyweight squats, scapular retraction holds.

  - 2–3 sessions per day of 1–2 minutes of nasal breathing to reduce sympathetic arousal and improve recovery quality.
